name: Jacob
overview: Jacob is the second-born son of Isaac and a male patriarch in the biblical narrative. He is notably recognized as the father of twelve sons who became the progenitors of the twelve tribes of Israel. His life is marked by significant divine encounters and covenantal promises.
namesAndTitles: The name Jacob means 'follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel,' reflecting his birth circumstances. God later gave him the name Israel, meaning 'he struggles with G-d [El],' after a profound encounter, signifying his spiritual wrestling and covenant relationship. He is also referred to by titles such as 'Israel My servant' and 'Jacob My servant,' highlighting his role as God's chosen servant in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Jacob is the son of Isaac and Rebekah and the father of twelve sons, including Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, and the daughter Dinah. He had children with his wives Bilhah and Zilpah as well. These relationships establish him as the patriarch of the tribes of Israel.
scriptureSignificance: Jacob is a central figure in God's redemptive plan, chosen despite his imperfect character to carry forward the covenant promises given to Abraham and Isaac. His renaming to Israel signifies his unique role in God's unfolding purpose. Through his twelve sons, he fathered the tribes that form the nation of Israel, embodying God's electing grace and faithfulness.
